item.title: Thunder Thursdays — Thu Aug 13, 8:30 PM — One World Brewing – West
item.description:
One World West is excited to present a new Thursday Residency – Thunder Thursdays! A new project featuring the joint forces of Alex Bazemore and Hannah Ramsey, alongside Joey Remillard and JC Hannon of Strictly Liquid! Expect fresh sets each week, with new takes on old tunes from your favorite artists, and perhaps even some original tunes! We’ll be bringing out the BOOM!
See ya there!
$10 Cover
With two unique locations, built inside buildings that were previously cast aside, One World brews with the intention of fostering nourishing interaction and artistic cultural experiences. From live music to art shows, “One World Brewing” is born from the magic that happens when the whole becomes greater than the sum of its parts. Our taprooms are intersections for people of all walks of life and different corners of the globe, enjoying this time and place together. Check out our upcoming schedule: click here

item.title: COMING THIS SUNDAY | African Summer Dance Party with Adama and Les Amis — Fri Aug 14 — One World Brewing – West
item.description:
Adama Dembele is Bambara and was born in Ivory Coast, West Africa. He is a master djembefola that has performed for communities all over the world. Adama is a 33rd generation musician from his family and teaches the music and culture of West African djembe and balafon in Asheville. Adama formed Les Amis to perform his traditional West African songs in a modern format with electric guitar, electric bass, drum kit and saxophone. The fusion of these instruments with his traditional djembe and balafon produced a high-energy dance band that offers audiences a one of a kind world music experience. Les Amis features Steve Campbell on drums, JP Furnas on electric bass, Michael Jaffe on electric guitar, Ben Colvin on Saxophone and Adama Dembele on djembe, balafon and vocals.
$10 Cover Outside show weather permitting With two unique locations, built inside buildings that were previously cast aside, One World brews with the intention of fostering nourishing interaction and artistic cultura

item.title: MST: Greybeard Overlook to Balsam Gap — Mon Aug 17, 8:30 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group Start at Greybeard Overlook, hike to Glassmine Falls Overlook, then on to the Balsam Gap parking area (aka Walker Knob) at the Big Butt trailhead, which is our break and our turn around.
Distance is about 7.5 miles, elevation (lowest point to highest point) is about 800 feet. Lots of up and down means total elevation is greater. Higher elevation means cooler weather.
Kudos to the CMC Monday Crew for recently weed-whacking the trail, parts of which were very overgrown when I scouted it last month.
Car pool: Meet at Folk Art Center, lower parking level at 8:30. Car pool is not mandatory. The drive to Greybeard Overlook is about 35 minutes.
Source: Asheville Hiking Group

item.title: Dupont: Corn Mill Shoals & Cedar Rock Mountain – 9.6 miles 1300' elevation — Wed Aug 19, 8:00 AM
item.description:
The Asheville Hiking Group **NOTE: EARLIER START TIME** How to find us: Mills River Ingles, 3338 Boylston Hwy, in front of gas pumps, closest to Boylston Hwy. Departing on time---8:00. Car pool to trailhead. (Second meeting site: Corn Mill Shoals parking lot, Dupont--about 8:30)
**Directions to Mills River Ingles**: I-26 Exit on NC-280 West, Airport Road---4.3 miles to the Ingles on the right.
**Details**: Varied terrain from gravel to smooth rock to groomed trails. Moderate ascents and descents with good footing. Mostly shaded, but some exposure. Loop 1: Wilkie to Micajah to Rock Quarry with an in-and-out to see rock formations, then Buck Ridge. Loop 2: Micajah to Rock Quarry to Twixt to Longside. Loop 3: Big Rock to Cedar Rock to Little River. Loop 4: Corn Shoals, then an in-and-out to Little River for a snack break, then Burnt Mountain to Corn Shoals and the cars. Type: 4 loops. Ascent: 1350’. Max elev: 3100’. Avg moving pace: 2.4 mph. Difficulty (1=effortless, 10=hard): 6.5. Dogs

item.title: Guided Trail Walk — Sat Aug 29, 10:00 AM
item.description: Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center.

item.title: Mushroom and Snail Sculpting Workshop — Sat Aug 29, 12:00 PM
item.description:
Mushroom and Snail Sculpting Workshop with Eileen Bos Saturday, August 29 | 12 – 4pm Register Here!
We will be hand sculpting 2 elements with several different materials for this class! Our mushrooms will begin with a foil base, which we will be covering in polymer clay & then baking. Once our mushrooms are baked, we will paint them with acrylic paints. From there, to create our snails, we will be using an air dry clay that is flexible after it is dry, called “Flower Clay” by Nara. Each snail will be adorned with a real snail shell. Once complete, your finished piece can decorate a special spot in your home, or be placed into a terrarium for safe keeping. Eileen Bos is a multimedia sculpture artist from NY, with nearly 40 years of self-taught art experience. She began drawing at the age of 3 and sculpting at age 4. item.title: Birding for Beginners — Tue Sep 1, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Birding for Beginners with Shane Myers Tuesday, September 1 | 9 – 10:30am BRN – Elective Register Here!
Join us on this birding walk around the NC Arboretum gardens and trails in search of our most colorful residents. We will go over best practices for using binoculars, recommendations for purchasing your own binoculars, and popular field guides to use. Bring your own binoculars but if you do not have a pair we have some loaner binoculars available to use during the program. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio. He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies

item.title: Weekly Critique — Wed Sep 2, 6:00 PM
item.description:
AVL Writers This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.
For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.
Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.
If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.
If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).
Source: AVL Writers
